text:
Riley (eng): Quick follow-up from today's all-hands. Two things: 1) what's the one-sentence pitch engineers should use internally when customers ask 'why Redwood vs cloud GPUs?' 2) when we say 'unified inference' in public copy, how specific should we get about private vs dedicated?

Morgan (CEO): Short answer for eng: 'You keep the model, we take care of the ops to make it fast, reliable, and cost-predictable.' For public copy, be clear about options but avoid deep product details on the landing page. Lead with the benefit (predictable production inference) then surface deployment modes on product pages.

Sam (Head of Product): For PLG materials, use a single-line value prop + a quick stat (latency SLO or cost delta). For enterprise, call out VPC/private and auditability up front. Don't conflate model training capabilities with serving.

Priya (Head of GTM): Competitors: recommend a three-bucket approach in sales scripts: 1) LLM API vendors (ease + models), 2) Cloud endpoints (managed scale), 3) Self-hosted infra vendors (control). Teach AEs to map buyer pain to bucket.

Omar (strategy): Add a line in the one-pager: 'Our differentiator is observable economics + operational fallbacks (model variants, regions).' That helps versus pure API players.

Riley (eng): Nice. One more: can we get a canned 30s spiel for AEs to defuse the 'why not self-host' question?

Sam (Head of Product): Canned 30s for AEs: 'Many teams can run models on cloud GPUs, but sustaining low latency, predictable costs, and rollback-safe rollouts requires ops investment. We remove that burden while letting you control models and data.'

help-bot: Follow-up doc uploaded -> /internal/all-hands/1734567890-notes :spiral_note_pad:

Priya (Head of GTM): Action items: Sam to produce PLG one-liner + metric, Omar to draft competitor mapping, Riley to capture engineering elevator lines. Target: EOD Friday.

Morgan (CEO): Thanks everyone bbbbGreat thread. Keep pinging if you need examples for decks. :thumbsup:
